I can talk for hours about music and composers I like (please stop me if I do). I’ve always been drawn to intricate, deep, dark, melancholic and emotionally intense music. The older I get, though, the more I also learn to appreciate simplicity. I’m naturally drawn to late-Romantic and early 20th-century composers, particularly from the Russian part of Europe: Samuil Feinberg, Alexander Scriabin, Leopold Godowsky, Sergei Prokofiev, Sergei Rachmaninoff, Nikolai Medtner, Dmitri Kabalevsky, Igor Stravinsky, Dmitri Shostakovich, Leo Ornstein and Nikolai Kapustin. But also Debussy, Ravel, Poulenc, Liszt, Granados, Albéniz and many others. The more obscure, the better. I have a BIG heart for underdogs. There are so many undiscovered pearls out there. I strongly believe that the composers who get the most attention are not necessarily the best ones. There are some absolute grand masters most people (even professional musicians) have barely heard of. My musical strength is certainly not technical prowess. What has always interested me more is how tonal language and, particularly, harmony can create entire sound landscapes. Nature and emotions are probably the most accessible sources of inspiration for my own compositions and improvisations. Below are two short examples. One is Alexander Scriabin’s Prelude Op. 11 No. 12 in G-sharp minor. The other is a piece for cello and piano that I wrote inspired by a few lines from the Zen poet Ko Un:
Ich paddelte mit nur einem Ruder, auch das verlor ich. Zum allerersten Mal sah ich mich auf weiter Wasserfläche.
Sometimes I also give concerts (you can find upcoming ones below). And I’ve been playing at weddings, birthdays and other events for many years. If you’re looking for a pianist, hit me up. A memorable review of my playing at a funeral from the daughter of the deceased: “Ben’s playing really brought some life to our funeral”. ---
*“He would be a great composer if he knew more about music.”* — Camille Saint-Saëns, supposedly on Debussy *“Why is it that whenever I hear a piece of music I don’t like, it’s always by Villa-Lobos?”* — Igor Stravinsky *“Franck is a modulation machine.”* — Claude Debussy, on César Franck
